newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany suspends Bosnia embassy contacts.
newsitem.headline: Germany suspends Bosnia embassy contacts.

text.p: Germany on Sunday became the first government to declare a suspension of contacts with Bosnia's envoys abroad after a recommendation made by the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp.
"As from yesterday, there has been an official freezing of contacts," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a statement.

Westendorp told reporters in Sarajevo on Saturday that he had recommended to Western powers that no ambassador be treated as a legitimate representative of Bosnia until a law governing Bosnian ambassadorial appointments was agreed.
Bosnia's factions have not yet finally settled differences over how ambassadorial posts should be divided among Serbs, Croats, Moslems and others.

Western allies had threatened to impose penalties on the joint postwar government of Bosnia unless it reached agreement on that and two other key laws by Friday -- a deadline set by NATO at a summit in May in Sintra, Portugal.
Westendorp had said he had extended the deadline until Monday because on two of the laws, governing passports and citizenship, good progress had been made.
The German Foreign Ministry statement however cited only the Friday deadline in explaining its reasons for the move, adding that its patience had run out.

"Without any perceptible readiness by leaders in Bosnia to reach a self-supporting peace through joint efforts, all international efforts are being undermined. The international community cannot allow this," Kinkel said.
But the dispute is just one of a range of issues that in recent weeks have clearly added to the exasperation of the German Foreign Ministry with Bosnia.

Following a visit to the region, Kinkel last week demanded an end to the attacks on international organisations in the Serb-controlled part of Bosnia that have followed increased efforts there to bring indicted war criminals to justice.

Kinkel said Serb-controlled Bosnia was increasingly isolating itself because former Bosnian Serb president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic was still at large and pulling political strings in the background.

The freeze on contacts with Bosnia's envoys in Germany will remain in place until Bosnia has managed to reach agreement on its ambassadorial appointments, the German Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
